subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should OpenClaw support PowerShell `$...` expansion tokens in Windows exec by routing them through explicit one-shot approval, or should it document script-file/direct-command usage as the supported contract?
rationale: The current source rejects expansion tokens in approval analysis, while changing that behavior affects command approval, auto-review, reusable trust, and command rendering rather than being a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Support one-shot expansion approval
options.body: Accept the direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 once it has redacted live Windows/Gateway proof and keep reusable `allow-always` unavailable for expansion-bearing commands.

options.title: Document the limitation
options.body: Reject inline expansion support for now and update the exec docs/tool guidance to make script files or direct non-wrapper commands the supported Windows path.

options.title: Defer to shell override design
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation behind the broader shell-selection/product decision in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49931.

recommendation.title: Support one-shot expansion approval
recommendation.body: Accept the direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 once it has redacted live Windows/Gateway proof and keep reusable `allow-always` unavailable for expansion-bearing commands.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice crosses Windows shell defaults, exec security policy, and approval UX; steipete appears in the relevant shell history and is the strongest available routing owner.
